QUESTIONS\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1. The sensitivity of diagnosing BPH or prostatomegaly by ultrasound?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBPH appears in TRUS as an echogenic and non-mobile mass. TRUS is mainly used to assess prostate volume, which is crucial for therapeutic strategies. Prostate volume can be estimated by serial planimetry, orthogonal plane, rotational body (single plane, ellipsoid) and three-dimensional methods.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EStaging sensitivities in studies using grey-scale TRUS varied between 30% and 50% with specificities between 77% and 96%. Three-dimensional TRUS aided in the assessment of extracapsular extension and seminal vesicle invasion.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2. How does hypothyroidism affect urine retention?\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn hypothyroidism there is loss of medullary hypertonicity impairing urinary concentration ability of kidneys . In hypothyroidism there is a reversible increase in vasopresssin sensitivity causing increased water reabsorbption\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3. What are the\u0026nbsp; causes of\u0026nbsp; external rotation of lower limbs ?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUnopposed pull on iliopsoas muscle which is attached to lesser trochanter or femoral retroversion\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4.How can u differentiate urinary retention from renal failure ?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn renal failure urine production is decreased thus there is requirement of dialysis whereas in urinary retention urine output is seen on catheterization\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"replies","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/vinilabhavani.blogspot.com\/feeds\/5515501204312746049\/comments\/default","title":"Post comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 63 yr old male resident of Ramanpeta a retired accountant came to the OPD with\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINTS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Edecreased urine output since 1 day\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShortness of breath since 1 day\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 1day ago when he developed decreased urine output which was sudden in onset, associated with urgency and pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe has shortness of breath since 1 day which is sudden in onset gradually progressive aggravated on walking and relieved by taking rest.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of abdominal distention and facial puffiness on and off since 3 months.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of fever, chest pain, palpitations, cough and back\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKnown case of hypothyroidism since 1 yr\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of diabetes mellitus, epilepsy, asthma .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETREATMENT Thyronorm for hypothyroidism\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPercutaneous Coronary Intervention stenting was done for CAD.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of haemorrhoidectomy 8 years back.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBefore illness : mixed diet, normal appetite, adequate sleep, regular bowel and bladder movements and no
